clue.text: Depict stern problem

parts.note: to draw a scene is to depict it
the stern of a boat is its back

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to portray a grave difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like an adjective meaning severe, but it is the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage or snag, a synonym for a problem in a plan.

clue.text: Remove act, very loud

parts.note: to do is to act
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Cutting a noisy turn from a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' reads as a stage turn but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff is to take off a garment, especially a hat, so it means remove.

clue.text: Right in strange way? Wrong

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the rearranged word
strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Is it correct to behave oddly, or is it wrong?
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, so a plan gone awry has gone wrong.

clue.text: Symbol in music book linked to scales played with frequency

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: played suggests notes run through in a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
F is the symbol for frequency

explanation.surface: A music textbook with scales practised again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass clef is the sign on a stave fixing F below middle C, used for low notes.

clue.text: Typical letter, one with endless criticism

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter of the criticism word is cut off

parts.note: a character is a letter or symbol in writing
I is the Roman numeral for one
to get stick is to receive criticism

explanation.surface: A standard letter of complaint that goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' is informal British for harsh criticism or teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristic describes what is distinctive and usual for someone, an adjective meaning typical of them.

clue.text: List of charges made by revolutionary artist in quarrel

indicators.note: the turned artist sits inside the word for a quarrel

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

indicators.note: a revolutionary turns things over, so the artist's letters are read the other way round

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A price list drawn up by a rebel painter in the middle of a spat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or duties, a published table of charges.

clue.text: Gold, smart colour

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to smart is to sting or burn

explanation.surface: Gold is a stylish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective meaning stylish, but it is the verb to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown shade, mostly used of hair, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Cross I drew, covering boundaries of London airport

indicators.note: covering means lying over or around, so the drew word wraps round the edge letters

parts.note: taken as written
to lure is to draw someone in

indicators.note: boundaries are the edges, so only the first and last letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of London
the outside letters of airport

explanation.surface: An angry person sketches the perimeter of Heathrow or Gatwick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a drawn mark beside 'I drew', but it is the adjective for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-natured means bad-tempered and surly, matching cross in the sense of irritable.

clue.text: Rodent filmed swimming on river

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters float into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
the Ouse is an English river, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A small animal caught on camera paddling in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A field mouse is a small wild mouse of fields and woodland, a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Vegetable oil back here got recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
also part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Cooking oil returned here for recycling, with a vegetable on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' does double duty in the surface but its letters are fodder; 'recycled' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Head off in area covered with trees and everything

parts.note: a forest is a large wooded area
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone sets off into woodland with all their belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as setting out on a trip, but it means to prevent something by acting first.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent or block something by getting in first, just as heading it off does.

clue.text: Contradict opinion lacking force

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for force is dropped from the opinion

parts.note: a belief is an opinion held
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with a view that carries no weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To belie something is to show it to be false, so the word works as contradict or give the lie to.

clue.text: Delight about honour and support for hotel worker

indicators.note: about means going around, so the delight wraps round the honour

parts.note: to charm is to delight
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by an award and backing for hotel staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chambermaid is a woman employed to clean and tidy bedrooms in a hotel.

clue.text: Cheerful deputy, good and honest

parts.note: to be up is to be in good spirits
a stand-in is a substitute or deputy
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A cheery, decent and honest second-in-command.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstanding means respectable and of good character, which suits honest.

clue.text: New study breaking dictator down

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these parts go into the ruler

parts.note: a despot is an absolute ruler
N is the abbreviation for new
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: Fresh research brings a tyrant low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' sits at the end like part of 'breaking down', but it is the definition, meaning sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondent means dejected and low in spirits, the same as feeling down.

clue.text: Current appeal about election's first posted by Democrat

indicators.note: about means going around, so the appeal surrounds everything that follows

parts.note: to pray is to make an earnest appeal

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word election

parts.note: the opening letter of election
a posted letter is sent
D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat

explanation.surface: A modern-day plea concerning a vote, mailed out by a party member.
explanation.definitionFit: Present-day describes what exists now, so it works as an adjective meaning current or contemporary.

clue.text: Total love for wrestling

parts.note: a sum is a total
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly devoted to the sport of grappling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total love' reads as complete devotion, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the traditional Japanese style of wrestling between heavy fighters in a ring.

clue.text: Very bad times for small communities

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects
ages are eras or times

explanation.surface: Hard times are hitting small rural places.
explanation.definitionFit: Villages are small settlements in the countryside, groups of houses smaller than towns.

clue.text: Time needed by mimic to make record

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: An impressionist needs time before cutting a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to record it, from recording sound or video onto magnetic tape.

clue.text: Attractive quality in crowd containing alien element

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the crowd word encloses the next two parts

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd of people
ET is the film's extraterrestrial
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Something appealing found in a crowd that includes an extraterrestrial ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Prettiness is the noun for being pleasing to look at, an attractive quality.

clue.text: Calm people agree

definitions.meaning: second meaning: populate, as colonists do a land
third meaning: decide or agree on terms

explanation.surface: Peaceful folk come to an accord.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one verb; 'people' is the verb to populate, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb works as soothe, as colonise a territory, and as reach an agreement on a deal or dispute.

clue.text: Silly distortion of online scans

indicators.note: a distortion twists something out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A daft garbling of documents scanned on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsensical means absurd or making no sense, an exact synonym for silly in this use.

clue.text: Open ground occupied in part

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the following words is used, running across them

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Land that was taken over is partly available.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a parcel or button is to unfasten it, so it means open.

clue.text: Hour in great discomfort

indicators.note: the hour letter goes inside the word for great

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Sixty minutes of real suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain, a form of bodily discomfort.

clue.text: Home movie's last part lacking skill

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: last asks for only the closing letter of the word movie

parts.note: the final letter of movie
PT is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: The closing section of a home video is amateurish.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or incompetent, so it describes someone without ability or skill.

clue.text: Nervous on airing composition initially devoid of life

indicators.note: something nervous is jittery and unsettled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word composition

parts.note: the opening letter of composition

explanation.surface: A jittery composer whose new piece, at its first broadcast, falls flat and lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic matter is not derived from living organisms, so it is without life.

clue.text: Understand article in newspaper after reflection

indicators.note: the article goes inside the newspaper word
a reflection shows things mirrored, so the newspaper word is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
the definite article

explanation.surface: Grasping a news story only after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' looks like careful thought, but it is a mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather something is to infer or understand it, as in 'I gather you were away'.

clue.text: Island's sound central element

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys; with the possessive S
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: The good sound of an island is what holds it all together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central wedge at the top of an arch, and figuratively the principal part of anything.
